cards.title: Accops Solutions for Government: Zero Trust Reference Architecture (V1, 2026)
cards.key_problem: A government department modernising its IT security needs one reference architecture covering private application access, identity, desktops, internet isolation, file transfer, remote support and endpoints - not seven separate product pitches it has to assemble itself.
key_outcomes: Seven integrated components presented as one Zero Trust reference architecture
Four ZTNA deployment options including reverse-connect with no inbound ports
Support for external QRNG for post-quantum cryptography
Web application protection against OWASP Top 10, OWASP Top 20 and SANS Top 25
Self-hosted or as-a-service delivery, cloud or on-premises
cards.brief: The newest government asset and the most complete architectural document in the demo set. It presents seven integrated components as a single Zero Trust design: ZTNA for private application access, HyID for MFA, SSO and IAM, the VDI suite, Remote Browser Isolation for internet access, AirBridge for secure file transfer, Huddle for remote support, and HyDesk thin clients. Each carries capabilities, a reference architecture and use cases. The ZTNA section is the most detailed, with four deployment options - on-premises or cloud, each with direct-connect or reverse-connect using Edge and App Connectors, the latter needing no inbound firewall openings - and two commercial models, self-hosted or ZTNA-as-a-service.
cards.use_for: Any government or public-sector opportunity, especially a tender or RFP needing a full architecture rather than a product datasheet. The entry document for a government deal.
cards.internal_reason: Proposed reference architecture for government security infrastructure. No public URL confirmed.

cards.title: Accops for Defence: Zero Trust for Air-Gapped and Mission-Critical IT (V4, Nov 2025)
cards.key_problem: Armed forces operate across border areas and sensitive zones on air-gapped networks, with high insider-threat risk and a need for data sovereignty, while still having to give contractors, temporary staff and OEM personnel controlled access.
key_outcomes: Six-solution stack mapped to defence use cases and deployment scenarios
Post-quantum cryptography with QRNG integration on the access gateway
Works over satcom and 3G/4G/5G tactical networks
Collapses the two-desktops-per-desk model to one using VDI
16 AV engines plus CDR for any file crossing the air gap
cards.brief: The defence-sector cut of the platform, organised as a stack table mapping each product to use cases, benefits and deployment scenarios. Named scenarios are concrete and sector-specific: command and control centres, DR and COOP sites, SOC and NOC, examination labs, forward units, ships, submarines, mobile command posts, secure briefing rooms and inter-agency collaboration zones. Distinctive claims are post-quantum cryptography with QRNG integration, operation over satellite and cellular tactical networks, tri-services information sharing, and the cost argument of replacing two desks-worth of hardware with one VDI endpoint. Virtual Browser with AirBridge handles the air-gap crossing, with 16 antivirus engines and Content Disarm and Reconstruction on every file.
cards.use_for: Defence, paramilitary and critical-infrastructure opportunities, particularly air-gapped environments or anywhere post-quantum readiness is being asked about.
cards.internal_reason: Describes security architecture for defence deployments. Not for general distribution.

cards.title: Gartner Magic Quadrant for Desktop as a Service, 11 August 2025
cards.key_problem: A prospect running a formal DaaS evaluation wants the analyst view of where every vendor sits, including the ones Accops is competing against, and including the criticisms of Accops.

cards.brief: The full 40-page Gartner Magic Quadrant for Desktop as a Service, published 11 August 2025, covering every vendor in the market. Accops appears as a Niche Player and newly meets the inclusion criteria. Gartner records the installed base as 90% Asia, 5% North America, 5% Europe, with top verticals in consulting and business services, financial services, and technology and telecom. Three strengths are named: operations automation and the JioPC offering, viability through Reliance Jio ownership, and unusually flexible licensing across perpetual, subscription, named, concurrent and device models. Two cautions are named: support outside India, the Middle East and Japan depends on channel partners, and Accops holds ISO 27001 but no other compliance certificates. Also the authoritative source on where every competitor sits.
cards.use_for: A formal DaaS evaluation, and internally as the honest picture of how an analyst sees Accops. Read the Cautions before a compliance-heavy deal - they name exactly what procurement will ask about.
cards.third_party_copyright: Gartner, Inc. Document G00822536. Licensed Gartner research - reprint rights are required before any external distribution, and Gartner citation policy governs quoting the placement.

cards.title: Accops ZTNA with Vajra Secure Enterprise Browser for BPM Organisations
cards.key_problem: BPM agents handle customer PII and financial data from home, on BYOD machines and through offshore teams, and one screenshot, copy-paste or screen-share can breach compliance or lose a client contract.
key_outcomes: DLP enforced at browser-render level, not just the network edge
600+ granular controls available in the Vajra secure browser
Vajra runs alongside the agent's normal browser, leaving personal use untouched
Accops File Encryption so only authorised apps can read files in-session
Auto-clear of cache, cookies, history, typed URLs and Recycle Bin at logout
cards.brief: The newest solution brief and the first document in the demo set covering Vajra, the Chromium-based secure enterprise browser. It pairs HySecure as the Zero Trust gateway with Vajra as the rendering surface, so that clipboard, screenshot, USB, printing, watermarking and session controls are enforced both at the endpoint and inside the browser content itself, with over 600 granular controls. The design point it makes repeatedly is coexistence: Vajra runs alongside Chrome or Edge rather than replacing them, so saved passwords and personal browsing are unaffected - which is what makes it viable on a BYOD or home machine. The access flow is agent device, Workspace Client authentication and posture check, HySecure gateway, then the published application only.
cards.use_for: BPM, BPO and contact-centre opportunities, and any deal where agents handle regulated data on machines the customer does not control. The strongest asset for a client-MSA or PCI-DSS agent-desktop requirement.
cards.internal_reason: Proposal-stage solution brief. No public URL confirmed.

cards.title: Accops Spectra with HySecure ZTNA: Device-Aware BYOD Compliance for BPM
cards.key_problem: A BPM's customer holds it accountable for the security of employee-owned laptops it does not own or manage, but full MDM enrolment on a personal device is intrusive, resisted and costly at BPM scale.
key_outcomes: HySecure gates access on whether the Spectra agent is present and tenant-registered
Gives the BPM's customer a verifiable real-time device-trust signal
Lightweight agent installs in minutes - no corporate imaging or full MDM
HySecure can call the Spectra Cloud API for live device health
Catches missing AV/EDR and pending OS updates before they become incidents
cards.brief: A solution brief introducing Spectra, Accops' unified endpoint management platform, as the device-trust signal for ZTNA access. The problem it solves is contractual rather than purely technical: a BPM's customer needs assurance about BYOD endpoints it cannot see, and the BPM cannot impose full MDM on personal machines. The answer is a new HySecure compliance check that verifies the Spectra agent is installed and actively registered to the BPM's specific Spectra tenant before the session proceeds, with an optional API call for live health and compliance state. The BPM gets fleet visibility - inventory, patch and AV telemetry - on devices it does not own, and the customer gets a device-trust signal it can verify.
cards.use_for: A BPM or outsourcing deal where the end customer is asking for BYOD device assurance, and any conversation where full MDM has been rejected as too intrusive.
cards.internal_reason: Proposal-stage solution brief describing a customer-specific compliance check. No public URL confirmed.

cards.title: Accops AirBridge: Secure File Transfer for Air-Gapped Networks (Technical Datasheet)
cards.key_problem: Air-gapped networks still need files to cross the gap for compliance submissions and collaboration, and the usual method - manually sanitised USB drives - is slow, unlogged and the most common way malware gets in.
key_outcomes: 8 or 16 antivirus engines scan every file
Content Disarm and Reconstruction across over 100 file types
Strips macros, embedded scripts, active content and metadata while preserving format
Separate Public Vault and Internal Vault file stores
Single-use download links delivered by email notification
cards.brief: The technical datasheet for AirBridge, a policy-controlled gateway for moving files between isolated networks - typically an internet-facing PC and an air-gapped LAN or OT network. Every file passes 8 or 16 antivirus engines plus Content Disarm and Reconstruction, which supports over 100 file types and strips macros, embedded scripts, active content and metadata before reconstructing the file with its format intact. Uploads from each side land in separate vaults, transfer policy keys off user identity, file type, size and source IP, and infected files go to quarantine. Users reach it three ways: a right-click context menu agent on either PC, a web portal, or a tray agent. It integrates with the Accops Remote Virtual Browser so a file downloaded inside the isolated browser flows into AirBridge automatically.
cards.use_for: Any air-gapped or OT environment that needs controlled file movement, and as the companion to Virtual Browser in a government or defence architecture.
cards.internal_reason: No public URL confirmed. Product literature with no customer detail - candidate for publication.

cards.title: Safe Internet Surfing Using Browser Isolation: Security Architecture Analysis
cards.key_problem: Signature-based endpoint security cannot stop polymorphic malware or an APT that establishes itself before detection, so physical network isolation alone is not enough to make internet access safe.
key_outcomes: Peer-reviewed: presented at ISA PPPA 2020, distributed with permission by ISA
Authored by Vijender Yadav, CTO of Accops
Argues multi-tiered endpoint security over perimeter-only strategy
Remote virtual browser keeps browsing productive while isolating the threat
Covers website tracking and demographic profiling as an attack enabler
cards.brief: The architectural argument beneath the Virtual Browser product, and the only externally peer-reviewed document in the demo set - presented at ISA PPPA 2020 and distributed with permission by ISA, authored by Accops CTO Vijender Yadav. It argues that signature-based antivirus fails against polymorphic malware and against attackers who establish presence before detection, so organisations must move from a perimeter-centric strategy to multi-tiered endpoint security. Remote browser isolation is then analysed as the mechanism: execute web content away from the endpoint so a compromise has nothing durable to compromise, while keeping browsing usable. It also covers website tracking and demographic profiling as a precursor to targeted attacks on individuals and their employers.
cards.use_for: A technical or security-architecture audience that wants the reasoning rather than a product pitch. The ISA presentation gives it third-party credibility the brochures do not have.
cards.stale_risk: Written November 2019 and presented in 2020, so it is roughly seven years old. The security argument holds, but any product capability described in it should be checked against the current Virtual Browser document rather than quoted from here.
cards.internal_reason: Distributed with permission of the authors by ISA - republication terms sit with ISA. No Accops public URL confirmed.

cards.title: Digital Colonization: How Foreign-Controlled Access Layers Threaten India's Network Security
cards.key_problem: If a foreign cloud-delivered ZTNA platform sits at the front door of Indian government networks, the ability to keep those systems running during sanctions or diplomatic pressure rests with overseas compliance teams rather than with New Delhi.
key_outcomes: Nayara Energy case study: Microsoft cut services to Indian energy infrastructure
Argues ZTNA is service architecture built on decades-old components, not proprietary code
Argues cloud-delivered ZTNA is more vulnerable than on-premises, not less
Cites India Stack as 20+ years of sovereign on-premises government infrastructure
Sets the policy direction against China's January 2026 approach, EU GAIA-X and US federal precedent
cards.brief: The newest whitepaper and the most strategic document in the set - a digital sovereignty argument authored by Accops CEO and CTO Vijender Yadav, dated December 2025. Its thesis is that identity, ZTNA and network-access layers are strategic infrastructure, and that adopting foreign cloud-delivered ZTNA in front of ministries, PSUs and defence-linked systems creates a kill-switch dependency. It builds the case from documented incidents, including Microsoft cutting off Nayara Energy, US sanctions affecting Indian companies, and extraterritorial legal reach under the CLOUD Act, then makes the technical argument that ZTNA is an assembly of long-established components rather than proprietary innovation, so there is no capability reason to import it. It closes with India Stack as precedent, the strength of the Indian vendor ecosystem, and a recommended policy direction benchmarked against China, the EU's GAIA-X and US federal practice.
cards.use_for: Government, PSU and policy conversations, and any deal where a foreign cloud ZTNA vendor is the competition. This is the sovereignty argument, not a product pitch - use it with a CISO or policy audience rather than a technical buyer.
cards.internal_reason: Takes a strong public-policy position and names foreign vendors adversarially in a geopolitical context. Distribution is a judgement call for Siddharth, not a default.
